page0.text:
...It's morning.
It's after seven o'clock.
The weather is nice outside, and bright white sunlight pours in.

page1.text:
"Mm...hup."
I get up and stretch my back.
Physically, I feel well.
I can move my limbs easily, and there's no trace of any headache.
I feel great waking up today, as if the horror of last night never happened.

page2.text:
"...Must have just been heartburn."
I sigh and think back on what happened.
...Even if I was reliving what happened ten years ago, I really need to train more if I can't remember anything that happened.
My memories since collapsing in the park are vague. All I remember is leaning on Saber's shoulder and being put to bed.

page3.text:
"Oh, right. I need to thank Saber."
I get out of bed and quickly change into my school uniform.

page4.text:
Saber seems like she's still asleep, so I'll go have breakfast.
It's already seven, so I should go see if Sakura's in the living room.

page5.text:
"S-Senpai."
In the living room, I find Sakura holding her school bag.
Breakfast is ready.
The table is neatly arranged and ready for us to start dining right away.

page6.text:
"Oh, is breakfast ready already?"
"Ah, yes. I had time, so I made enough for you and Saber, too."

page7.text:
"? But what about your food?"
"Um... I'll be okay. I'm going to school first, so please enjoy your breakfast."

page8.text:
"...?
What's wrong, Sakura? It's weird that you made us breakfast, yet you aren't going to have any... Did something happen yesterday?"

page9.text:
...Sounds like I was on the mark.
But I can't think of anything from yesterday's events that would apply.
After dinner last night, Sakura went back to her room, and that was the last time I saw her.
After that...I think something happened, but the thought gives me so much nausea that I can't remember.

page10.text: "Oh, come to think of it, I remember talking with you and Saber about something."

page11.text:
"...I said something terrible. When I saw you nearly unconscious, I lost my temper."
"You said something to Saber?"

page12.text:
"...Yes. Something that I had no right to say. It pinned all the blame on Saber.
...So, I can't really look her in the eye right now."
So that's why she made breakfast for two and is trying to leave before she runs into Saber.

page13.text: "...I'm sorry. I realized how stupid I was being and apologized to her right away. And then Saber apologized to me, too. She said she was careless, even though it was all my fault."

page14.text:
Sakura hangs her head, looking ashamed.
...I see.
If you apologize to someone and they end up apologizing back to you, that would make you feel even worse.

page15.text:
"...You two are so silly. I'm obviously the one most responsible for getting myself hurt. You shouldn't argue over something like that."
"But Senpai, Saber didn't—"

page16.text:
"It's okay. I'll just say this now, but when she knows someone else is wrong, she doesn't back down. If you make a bad case to her, she'll get really mad at you. The fact that she apologized means that she accepts what you said.
Saber might not say it, but she likes you. She values people who try their best."

page17.text:
"...Yes. That's all the more reason I'm avoiding her this morning.
Since Saber didn't scold me, I need to be harder on myself or else it'll get to my head."
Sakura laughs bashfully and gives me a modest bow.
Looks like her mind is set on leaving for school early.

page18.text: "...If you insist, then I won't stop you. But what are you going to do so early in the morning? Practice is cancelled."

page19.text:
"It's okay, I can just clean the dojo. After what I said to Saber, it's only right that I scrub the floors as penance."
Sakura bids me farewell and leaves the living room.

page20.text:
"Cleaning the dojo? It's really hard to scrub the floors in the winter, you know."
...She knows that as well as I do, though, which is probably why she said it.
I wonder what she said to pick a fight with Saber, if she thinks she has to do such an unenviable task to make up for it.
